clue.text: Sport new to the Spanish smoker?

parts.note: sport in the sense of amusement or play is fun
el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: A question about a Spanish smoker taking up a new sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smoker' is not a person but the thing a ship's smoke goes up through.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's or engine's chimney is the part that gives out smoke, so it can be called a smoker.

clue.text: Bloomer down phone

parts.note: feeling down is feeling blue, low in spirits
to give someone a bell is British slang for phoning them

explanation.surface: Someone made a blunder and is down on the phone about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a mistake (or a loaf), but here it is something that blooms. 'Give me a bell' is British for 'phone me'.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodland flower is a plant that blooms, so the crossword calls it a bloomer.

clue.text: 16 down's daughters must be kept in line

indicators.note: the daughters must be held within the word for line, so it wraps around them

parts.note: a file is a line, as in single file
D is the abbreviation for daughter, doubled for daughters

explanation.surface: A swindler's daughters have to be kept in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 down is CON, so the definition is a con, a swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindle or dishonest dodge is a fiddle in British slang, the same as a con.

clue.text: 17 that's a 16 down artist, say

indicators.note: say asks us to speak the phrase and take what it sounds like

parts.note: 16 down is CON, and a con artist is a cheater

explanation.surface: A cat described as a swindler of an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is CAT. 'Say' signals a soundalike: a con artist is a cheater, which said out loud is the name of the fast big cat.
explanation.definitionFit: The fastest land animal is a big spotted feline, so it is an example of a cat.

clue.text: 17 from first half of paper? Yes for the Berliner, primarily

indicators.note: primarily says the German yes comes first in the answer

parts.note: ja is German for yes, so a Berliner would say it

indicators.note: first half of keeps only the opening four of the eight letters of the newspaper's name

parts.note: the paper is the Guardian, the newspaper this crossword appears in

explanation.surface: A cat taken from the front pages of a newspaper, with a German nod to the Berliner format.
explanation.walkthrough: The Guardian was printed in the Berliner page size, so 'paper' and 'Berliner' both seem to be about newspapers; Berliner is really a German speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: The big spotted American feline is one of the great cats, matching 17, which is CAT.

clue.text: My boss during October only

indicators.note: during says the answer runs inside the words October only

explanation.surface: Someone says their boss is only around in October.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is Puck, and in A Midsummer Night's Dream Puck serves the fairy king, so 'My boss' is the setter speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's fairy king is Puck's master, and this puzzle's setter is called Puck.

clue.text: Spooner's busy wide bay is part of Spanish culture

indicators.note: Spooner's says the opening sounds of the two words are swapped

parts.note: a busy place is full
a bight is a wide curving bay

explanation.surface: A crowded broad bay is said to be a feature of Spanish life.
explanation.definitionFit: The ring spectacle with a matador is a traditional element of Spain's way of life.

clue.text: 17 flap to purchase, we hear

parts.note: a tab is a small flap

indicators.note: we hear says the word for purchase is taken by its sound

parts.note: to purchase is to buy

explanation.surface: A cat flap is for sale.
explanation.definitionFit: A striped domestic feline is an example of a cat.

clue.text: Less prepared to find one immersed in a French textbook

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: immersed in says the word for one sinks inside the other pieces

parts.note: a reader is a school textbook for reading
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone less ready for an exam finds themselves buried in a French textbook.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of not ready, meaning more poorly prepared than another.

clue.text: Like a 17 in light snowfall, when left out

indicators.note: out says the letter for left is dropped from the snowfall word

parts.note: a flurry is a light fall of snow

explanation.surface: A cat out in a light fall of snow.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat is covered in fur, so being hairy and soft is cat-like.

clue.text: Work featuring duck and Manx 17

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, the shape of the letter O

indicators.note: the Manx cat has no tail, so this one loses its last letter

parts.note: 17 is CAT, and puss is another word for a cat

explanation.surface: A piece of art featuring a duck and a tailless cat.
explanation.walkthrough: The Manx breed, from the Isle of Man, is tailless, so the cat loses its tail letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A composer's numbered composition is a work, from the Latin for work.

clue.text: 16 down's jumper, reportedly extremely cute

indicators.note: reportedly says the word for jumper is taken by its sound

parts.note: a flea is an insect that jumps

indicators.note: extremely picks the two outside letters of cute

explanation.surface: A con man's sweater is said to be very cute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' looks like a sweater, but it is a flea. 16 down is CON, used as a verb: to swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: To fleece someone is to swindle them out of money, the same as to con them.

clue.text: Dad is back at his job, that's clear

indicators.note: is back says the word for dad is turned round

parts.note: pa is an informal word for dad
a dad's job is being a parent

explanation.surface: A father has returned to work, plainly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obvious or plain to see is evident, which is what clear means here.

clue.text: See 16
See 16
Chris Hoy? On vacation, he's not really famous

indicators.note: on vacation empties the name, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: a C-list celebrity is barely famous, well below the A-list

explanation.surface: Chris Hoy, away on holiday, is not much of a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Chris Hoy is a British Olympic champion on the track bike, so the name does double duty.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish Olympic champion raced bikes on the track, so he is an example of a bike rider.

clue.text: Party animal, female, has male chained up?

parts.note: Con is short for the Conservative Party
a cat is an animal
Ena is a woman's name
Ted is a man's name

explanation.surface: A female party animal keeps a man tied up.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is itself built by joining short words end to end, which is what it means.
explanation.definitionFit: Linked together in a series, like links joined in a chain.

clue.text: See 16
16 down's small flower

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river: the Cam runs through Cambridge

explanation.surface: A con man's little flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a crossword favourite for a river; the Cam is the river of Cambridge. 16 down is CON.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindle or fraud is a con, a dishonest trick.

clue.text: On The Beach, showing in a London street

parts.note: the Strand is a famous street in central London

explanation.surface: The film On The Beach is showing at a cinema on a London street.
explanation.walkthrough: On The Beach looks like a film title, but it is the definition. The Strand is a major London street.
explanation.definitionFit: An old adverb meaning stranded on the shore, as Dickens used it.

clue.text: Journalist writing about beer

parts.note: re means about or concerning
porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: A journalist writing a piece about beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper writer who covers stories is a news gatherer, a kind of journalist.

clue.text: Old man entertained by frisky older 17

indicators.note: entertained by says the old man is taken in by the other pieces
frisky says the letters of older jump about into a new order

parts.note: an old man is a father, pa

explanation.surface: A father is entertained by a playful older cat.
explanation.definitionFit: The spotted big feline of Africa and Asia is one of the great cats.

clue.text: Tight Scot, seen heading off without a wallet

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the shuffled letters go round the a
tight means drunk, so the letters stagger into a new order
heading off removes the first letter of seen

explanation.surface: A mean Scot is spotted going off without his wallet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tight Scot' plays on the stereotype of the mean Scot, but 'Tight' (drunk) shuffles SCOT plus EEN into NOTECSE, and 'without' means outside, wrapping round A.
explanation.definitionFit: A pocket case for holding banknotes is a wallet.

clue.text: 17 in another clue too, but not for anyone to see

indicators.note: another means a different version, so the letters of clue too are rearranged

parts.note: a U certificate means a film anyone can see, so U is the letter taken away

explanation.surface: A cat hidden in another clue, kept from public view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' shuffles CLUE TOO, but U must come out first: U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for everyone, so 'not for anyone to see' removes it.
explanation.definitionFit: The spotted wild feline of the Americas is a kind of cat.

clue.text: Flag officer, Geordie, given lift by Leo?

indicators.note: in a down answer, given lift says the letters are raised, read bottom to top

parts.note: a Geordie comes from Newcastle in the North East of England, NE
Leo is a star sign

explanation.surface: A naval officer from Newcastle gets a lift from someone called Leo.
explanation.walkthrough: A flag officer is an admiral, but here 'Flag' and 'officer' each define the answer: it is both a flag and a junior officer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a naval flag and also a junior commissioned officer rank.

clue.text: 16 down by tearaway

parts.note: to rip is to tear
off means away, as in going off

explanation.surface: A swindle pulled by a young hooligan.
explanation.walkthrough: A tearaway is a reckless youth, but the word splits into tear and away. 16 down is CON.
explanation.definitionFit: An overpriced swindle or fraud is a con.

clue.text: Dinner 50% off? It's a 16 down

definitions.meaning: half of dinner is din, a loud noise, which is another word for this
16 down is CON, and a dishonest scheme is a con

explanation.surface: A half-price dinner deal turns out to be a swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is indirect: half of 'Dinner' is DIN, a loud noise, and the answer means din.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a loud din and a dishonest money-making scheme.

clue.text: Bits of info about English sides

indicators.note: about says the bits of info go around the English letter

parts.note: facts are bits of information

explanation.surface: Pieces of information about English matters.
explanation.definitionFit: The faces or aspects of a gem or problem are its sides.

clue.text: Former Man U player keeping a big 17, perhaps

parts.note: George Best was a famous Manchester United footballer

explanation.walkthrough: George Best was a star of Manchester United in the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: A lion or tiger, a large cat, is an example of a wild animal.

indicators.note: getting into says the word for one goes inside the shuffled letters
awful says the letters of scrape are badly jumbled

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards

explanation.definitionFit: The Cold War rivalry to reach the Moon and orbit was the superpowers' contest beyond Earth.

clue.text: 17, male, tough guy regularly left out

indicators.note: regularly left out drops every other letter of tough guy

explanation.surface: A cat, a man, and a hard man pushed aside.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for an ordinary house cat.

clue.text: Restaurateur on TV, judging pie Luther baked

indicators.note: baked says the letters of pie Luther are cooked into a new order

explanation.surface: A TV restaurateur judging a pie that Luther baked.
explanation.walkthrough: She is a judge on The Great British Bake Off, so 'judging' and 'baked' fit the scene.
